interpretation: Transposition certificates are finite instances of closed observation invariants, not an enumeration of all adaptive strategies.
Used deletion/query supports accumulate across the whole certification history and survive resets.
The cumulative covering trace is different from an individually shortest counterexample.
One-removal words may have arbitrary finite length; all post-removal lookups still only fix the removed correspondence.
Anchors are correct and given before a fresh complete-store experiment. Arbitrary correlated subfamilies and inherited partial stores can have lower costs.
Native-edge reconciliation composes retained observations and does not constitute a new continuous native run.

parameters.adaptive_scope: sound identity-certification branch; not identification of an arbitrary unknown permutation
parameters.family: every permutation fixing the supplied anchors
parameters.initial_store: all rows present, distinct unexpired tokens, one returned user
parameters.lifecycle: fixed clock, nonrenewing lookup, named-row removal
parameters.request_cost: one per lookup or removal; resets and supplied anchor discovery excluded
parameters.reset: restore the complete store; preserve binding and accumulated observations

results.individual_shortest_projected_witness: two requests for each nonidentity member

inherited_store.interpretation: The residual-cost theorem starts from the complete store, not a previously deleted store.

restricted_family.interpretation: The full remaining permutation family is necessary for the lower bound.
